questions.q_en:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the parts in the correct sequence to form a meaningful sentence.

(P) effective storytelling captivates audiences,

(Q) and fosters deeper connections

(O) conveys complex ideas simply,

(R) between people
questions.solution_en:
The sentence logically begins with part (P) "Effective storytelling captivates audiences,". This introduces the subject ("Effective storytelling") and the first verb phrase ("captivates audiences").

Part (O) "conveys complex ideas simply," presents a second action performed by "Effective storytelling." It is parallel to the first action in (P). So far: "Effective storytelling captivates audiences, conveys complex ideas simply,".

Part (Q) "and fosters deeper connections" adds a third action, connected by the conjunction "and." This continues the list of what effective storytelling does.

Part (R) "between people" is a prepositional phrase that modifies "connections," specifying the nature of these connections. It completes the idea presented in (Q).

Thus, the correct and meaningful order of the sentence is POQR.

The sentence formed after rearrangement is: Effective storytelling captivates audiences, conveys complex ideas simply, and fosters deeper connections between people.

Hence, the correct answer is option (b).

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

Marcel said, "I want a long vacation."
options_en: Marcel says that he wanted a long vacation.
Marcel said that he wanted a long vacation.
Marcel told to me that he wants a long vacation.
Marcel said that he wants a long vacation.
questions.solution_en:
The sentence in the Direct Speech is in Simple Present Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Indirect Speech should be in Simple Past Tense.

Simple Present (Subject +V1st + Object) should be converted into Simple Past (Subject +V2 + Object).

"That" is used in place of Inverted Commas while transforming the sentence from Direct Speech to Indirect Speech.

For example:

He said, "I never go to the village." (Direct Speech)

He said that he never went to the village. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

· The pronoun 'I' is changed into 'he'.

· The verb 'want' (simple present) is changed into 'wanted' (simple past).

None of the options except (b) follows these rules. Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Marcel said that he wanted a long vacation.

Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

options_en: This year, I have to crack SSC CGL.

SSC CGL will have to be cracked by me this year.
questions.solution_en:

·The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive Voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

·The usage of a helping verb is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

·The preposition "by" is used before the object made in Passive Voice. However, it is optional in some cases.

·The question in Active voice is in Infinitive form.

·Infinitive sentence is: To + V1 form.

·The format in Active voice is: Subject + am/is/are/was/were + to + V1 + object

·Thus, the format in Passive voice will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + am/is/are/was/were + to + be + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

·For example:

o I have to lend some books. (Active)

o Some books have to be lent by me. (Passive)

Option (b) is incorrect as the plural verb "have" cannot be used for the singular noun "SSC CGL".

·The options except (c) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

·Therefore, the correct answer is: SSC CGL has to be cracked by me this year.

d) Ignore - This means to refuse to take notice of or acknowledge. This is not related to hindering progress.

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

In the part of Italy that is known as Umbria, there stands the little town of Assisi, built on the slopes of Monte Subasio. Assisi is a very old city - some say it dates as far back as 400 or 500 B.C. - and underneath its streets are long passages that come out far away in the hills, as if the citizens had used them in times of siege as a means of escape. If you studied its ruins of temples, theatres, and circuses, you would learn a great deal of history, not only of Assisi itself but of Rome as well. Totila, the Goth, halted there for a short time on his way to besiege the Eternal City. This nickname would become symbolic of a remarkable future. Giovanni would grow up to transform not only his own life but also the lives of countless others, embodying values of humility and compassion that continue to resonate around the world.

Directions [Set of 4 Questions]:Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow.

Dog trainers typically describe their training methods on their websites. The scientists analysed these training philosophies to identify the words and phrases used by trainers to indicate different methods. Because 56 percent were ambiguous, they also looked at the tools used and at reviews. They classified the trainers as non-aversive (i.e., reward-based) or aversive. 55 percent of the trainers were classed as aversive, meaning they used aversive methods at least some of the time. The results showed that some words or phrases were pretty much only used by one kind of trainer, and never or rarely by the other. The exception was sometimes when a non-aversive trainer mentioned that they did not use a particular method. Aversive trainers sometimes described a "balanced approach" while non-aversive trainers wrote about positive reinforcement. Some words were used by both types of trainers but in different ways; for example, when aversive trainers referred to "tools" they meant concrete things like shock collars, whereas non-aversive trainers more often used this word to describe skills or knowledge that the dog's guardian would develop. Some phrases seem to always indicate an aversive trainer: electronic or e-collar, pack leader, and mother nature. And phrases that indicated a non-aversive trainer were shock collar (as in, they don't use them) and science. The words "electronic" and "shock" give different impressions of the same device.

One day, a very long time ago, some of the Naayire people went hunting. They walked and walked in the bush but found nothing. When night came, they were very far from home. "We must sleep in the bush," the chief said, "we must find a good place to sleep. "The hunters were not afraid to sleep in the bush. But they knew elephants, lions and other animals sometimes killed sleeping hunters. And there were some bad people, too, in the bush.

The hunters came to a place with big trees around it. They decided to rest and sleep on the grass. They did not make a fire and ate only some nuts which they carried in their bags. That was their supper. Then they went to sleep. All of them were tired. They slept soundly and did not hear anything. They did not hear that their enemies were coming nearer and nearer to them. But in one of the trees above the sleeping men, something moved and fell on the head of a young hunter. He jumped up and cried a big python was on his head!

The Naayire hunters got up quickly and saw the enemies around them. A fight began. Soon the enemies ran away and that was the end of the fight. The Naayire hunters came up to their chief to talk about the fight. "What made you jump up?" the chief asked the young hunter. "It was a python," he said. "It fell on my head, but it did not kill me." Then the chief said, "From this day on our people will never kill a python. That python saved our lives. Pythons will be sacred animals in our country." Even today the Naayire people love pythons. If you go into their houses in the rainy season, you will find a python there. The pythons never harm anyone. They don't eat even the chickens.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

The boy asked his father if he was returning home.
options_en: The boy said to his father, "Were you returning home?"
The boy said to his father, "Are you returning home?"
The boy said to his father, "Will you be returning home?"
The boy said to his father, "Should you returning home?"
questions.solution_en:
In the case of sentences like this where the sentence takes an Interrogative form in Direct Speech, "enquired (of)", "wanted to know", "asked", etc. in Indirect Speech is changed into "said" in Direct Speech.

In Direct speech, the verb is always placed before the subject, unlike in Indirect Speech.

If there is a question whose answer can come as "Yes" or "No", we should use "If" or "Whether" before the Indirect Speech and "Is/are/am/was/were" before the Direct Speech.

For example:

Kane asked him if he was doing well. (Indirect Speech)

Kane said to him, "Are you doing well?" (Direct Speech)

The tense of the Indirect Speech is in the Past Continuous Tense. So, the tense in the Direct Speech will be in the Present Continuous Tense.

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech:

Indirect SpeechDirect Speech
asked.. ifsaid to
He was returningAre you returning

From the given options, one that follows the above mentioned conditions for Direct speech is option (b) "The boy said to his father, "Are you returning home?""

Hence, the correct answer is option (b).

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate collocation to substitute the underlined phrase in the given sentence.

The citizens took to the streets, protesting of the government's decision to increase taxes.
questions.solution_en:
The verb "protest" is typically followed by the preposition "against" to indicate the target or subject of the protest. It conveys the idea that the citizens are demonstrating or expressing their dissatisfaction with the government's decision. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

The final sentence would be: The citizens took to the streets, protesting against the government's decision to increase taxes.
